title: Fully Quantum Algorithm for the 1-dimensional linear Lattice Boltzmann Method
authors: Mohammed Bediche, Matthijs van Waveren, Denis Ricot, Pierre Sagaut
abstract: A fully quantum algorithm for solving the one-dimensional linear advection-diffusion equation using the Lattice Boltzmann method as a numerical procedure is presented in this work. We start by presenting a state of the art of the current usage of quantum algorithms for solving ordinary and partial differential equations. We then describe two algorithms for the one-dimensional Lattice Boltzmann method with two degrees of freedom. The first one is an existing hybrid quantum-classical algorithm with measurements at each time step, and the second one is our improved version, viz. a fully quantum algorithm where only one measurement is needed at the end of the algorithm. The fully quantum algorithm is first executed on a quantum simulator and then compared with a classical approach. Subsequently, the fully quantum algorithm is run on a quantum system with 133 qubits to investigate the effect of noise and the depth of the circuit on the output state. We find fluctuations in the final result due to the decoherence noise of the qubits.
summary: The paper presents a novel, fully quantum algorithm for simulating the 1D advection-diffusion equation using the Lattice Boltzmann Method. It improves upon prior hybrid methods by eliminating time-step measurements, allowing for more efficient quantum evolution. The work validates the approach via simulation and tests its feasibility on current noisy quantum hardware.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a fully quantum algorithm capable of solving the one-dimensional linear advection-diffusion equation using the Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM). This aims to surpass the limitations of existing hybrid quantum-classical approaches.
main_result: The proposed fully quantum algorithm was successfully simulated on a quantum simulator, matching classical results. While testing on physical hardware showed expected decoherence noise fluctuations, it demonstrated the potential for a measurement-free time evolution step.
method: The work compares a hybrid quantum-classical scheme with an improved, fully quantum approach that minimizes measurements by encoding state information across time steps to calculate subsequent equilibrium distributions directly within the quantum circuit.
model_or_system: The simulation targets the 1D linear advection-diffusion equation solved via the LBM. The computational platform involves quantum circuits implemented on simulators and tested on a 133-qubit quantum processor.
key_observables: Particle density (rho) and fluid velocity (u), extracted from the final state vector $|\psiangle$.
important_parameters: The system size is defined by the number of lattice points ($N$), and time evolution involves discrete steps ($\Delta t$). The hardware test utilized a 133-qubit machine.
main_assumptions: The key assumption for improvement is that information can be retained quantum mechanically across time steps, bypassing the classical measurement bottleneck inherent in hybrid methods. Decoherence noise limits current hardware performance.
figures_summary: Figures compare the fully quantum algorithm's output against classical results on a simulator and show qualitative evolution matching classical expectations when run on physical quantum hardware (ibm_torino).
paper_structure: The paper first reviews the state-of-the-art in quantum algorithms for PDEs, then details the existing hybrid LBM approach. The core contribution is presenting and analyzing the fully quantum algorithm, followed by simulation results and hardware testing.
why_interesting: This work directly applies advanced quantum computation techniques (quantum walks, unitary evolution) to solve a fundamental problem in fluid dynamics, bridging theoretical quantum algorithms with practical condensed matter/fluid physics modeling.
